study type: Qualitative study using Focus Group Discussions
exposure: availability of care for perinatal depression
stigma and negative stereotypes by care providers towards adolescent pregnancy and perinatal depression
providers trained in the management of perinatal depression
outcome: health service utilization for adolescent perinatal depression
cohort: The study included low-income young mothers (who were adolescents at the time of a previous RCT and had medical histories of adolescent perinatal depression) and primary care clinicians treating this condition in Ibadan, Nigeria.
finding: Participants identified unsupportive and stigmatizing clinic environments towards pregnant and parenting adolescents as significant barriers to accessing available care, while availability of care, perceived health benefits, individual patient resilience, and trained providers were enabling factors.
cross-section timing: Focus Group Discussions were conducted in 2020, exploring participants' experiences related to the perinatal period between 2014 and 2016.
